title: LIGR-seq: Ligation-based RNA–RNA interaction mapping by in vivo crosslinking and proximity ligation
key_innovation: Compared with conventional RNA–RNA interaction mapping approaches, LIGR-seq introduces in vivo psoralen-mediated crosslinking combined with proximity ligation and strand-specific sequencing, enabling transcriptome-wide identification of RNA duplexes and intermolecular RNA–RNA interactions with nucleotide-level resolution in living cells.

blocks.text: How does LIGR-seq capture RNA–RNA interactions through psoralen crosslinking and proximity ligation?

blocks.alt: Overview of the LIGR-seq strategy for transcriptome-wide RNA–RNA interaction mapping
blocks.legend: **Figure 1. Overview of the LIGR-seq strategy for transcriptome-wide RNA–RNA interaction mapping.** LIGR-seq uses AMT-mediated psoralen crosslinking to stabilize RNA duplexes in living cells, followed by RNA fragmentation, proximity ligation, crosslink enrichment, and high-throughput sequencing. The resulting chimeric reads are computationally analyzed to identify significant RNA–RNA interactions and reconstruct cellular RNA interaction networks.
blocks.label: LIGR-seq F1

blocks.text: Can LIGR-seq identify known RNA duplex structures in living cells?

blocks.alt: Validation of LIGR-seq by detecting established RNA–RNA interactions
blocks.legend: **Figure 2. Validation of LIGR-seq by detecting established RNA–RNA interactions.** LIGR-seq recovers known spliceosomal snRNA interactions, including U2–U6 and U4–U6 RNA duplexes, demonstrating its ability to capture endogenous RNA helices and intermolecular RNA contacts in vivo.
blocks.label: LIGR-seq F2
